section_heading: Table: Capability Thresholds and Required Safeguards
locator: Table 1 / AI R&D / AI R&D-5 / Required Safeguards
context_stem: Row: Autonomous AI Research and Development (AI R&D), threshold AI R&D-5. Column: Required Safeguards.
excerpt: As with AI R&D-4, we also expect an affirmative case will be required.
paraphrase: Similar to AI R&D-4, an affirmative case is expected to be required for AI R&D-5.

excerpt: These Capability Thresholds represent our current understanding of the most pressing catastrophic risks.
paraphrase: The listed Capability Thresholds reflect Anthropic's current understanding of the most pressing catastrophic risks.

excerpt: As our understanding evolves, we may identify additional thresholds.
paraphrase: Additional thresholds may be identified as understanding evolves.

excerpt: For each threshold, we will identify and describe the corresponding Required Safeguards as soon as feasible, and at minimum before training or deploying any model that reaches that threshold.
paraphrase: Required Safeguards for each threshold will be identified as soon as feasible and no later than before training or deploying a model reaching that threshold.

excerpt: We will consider it sufficient to rule out the possibility that a model has surpassed the two Autonomous AI R&D Capability Thresholds by considering an earlier (i.e., less capable) checkpoint: the ability to autonomously perform a wide range of 2-8 hour software engineering tasks.
paraphrase: An earlier checkpoint — autonomous performance of 2-8 hour software engineering tasks — will suffice to rule out surpassing the AI R&D thresholds.

excerpt: We would view this level of capability as an important checkpoint towards both Autonomous AI R&D as well as other capabilities that may warrant similar attention (for example, autonomous replication).
paraphrase: This checkpoint capability is viewed as significant for both AI R&D and other concerning capabilities like autonomous replication.

excerpt: We will test for this checkpoint and, by the time we reach it, we will (1) aim to have met (or be close to meeting) the ASL-3 Security Standard as an intermediate goal;
paraphrase: Anthropic will test for this checkpoint and aim to have met or nearly met the ASL-3 Security Standard by that time.

context_stem: we will (1) aim to have met (or be close to meeting) the ASL-3 Security Standard as an intermediate goal;
excerpt: (2) share an update on our progress around that time; and (3) begin testing for the full Autonomous AI R&D Capability Threshold and any additional risks.
paraphrase: Anthropic also commits to sharing a progress update and beginning testing for the full AI R&D threshold and additional risks around that time.

excerpt: We will also maintain a list of capabilities that we think require significant investigation and may require stronger safeguards than ASL-2 provides.
paraphrase: Anthropic will maintain a watch list of capabilities that may need stronger-than-ASL-2 safeguards.

excerpt: This group of capabilities could pose serious risks, but the exact Capability Threshold and the Required Safeguards are not clear at present.
paraphrase: These capabilities could pose serious risks, though precise thresholds and safeguards are not yet defined.

excerpt: These capabilities may warrant a higher standard of safeguards, such as the ASL-3 Security or Deployment Standard.
paraphrase: These watch-list capabilities might require a higher standard such as ASL-3 Security or Deployment.

excerpt: However, it is also possible that by the time these capabilities are reached, there will be evidence that such a standard is not necessary (for example, because of the potential use of similar capabilities for defensive purposes).
paraphrase: It is also possible that evidence will eventually show a higher standard is unnecessary, for example if the capability can be used defensively.

excerpt: Instead of prespecifying particular thresholds and safeguards today, we will conduct ongoing assessments of the risks with the goal of determining in a future iteration of this policy what the Capability Thresholds and Required Safeguards would be.
paraphrase: Rather than fixing thresholds now, Anthropic will assess risks on an ongoing basis to define thresholds and safeguards in a future policy update.

excerpt: At present, we have identified one such capability:
paraphrase: Anthropic states it has currently identified one capability of this kind.

excerpt: Cyber Operations: The ability to significantly enhance or automate sophisticated destructive cyber attacks, including but not limited to discovering novel zero-day exploit chains, developing complex malware, or orchestrating extensive hard-to-detect network intrusions.
paraphrase: Cyber Operations capability is defined as significantly enhancing or automating sophisticated destructive cyber attacks, including zero-day discovery, malware development, and network intrusion.

context_stem: Row: Cyber Operations. Column: Ongoing Assessment.
excerpt: This will involve engaging with experts in cyber operations to assess the potential for frontier models to both enhance and mitigate cyber threats, and considering the implementation of tiered access controls or phased deployments for models with advanced cyber capabilities.
paraphrase: Ongoing assessment for Cyber Operations involves expert engagement and consideration of tiered access or phased deployment.

context_stem: Row: Cyber Operations. Column: Ongoing Assessment.
excerpt: We will conduct either pre- or post-deployment testing, including specialized evaluations.
paraphrase: Testing, including specialized evaluations, will occur either before or after deployment.

context_stem: Row: Cyber Operations. Column: Ongoing Assessment.
excerpt: We will document any salient results alongside our Capability Reports (see Section 3).
paraphrase: Salient cyber capability results will be documented alongside Capability Reports.

excerpt: We hope to publish updates approximately every 6 months.
paraphrase: Anthropic hopes to publish updates roughly every six months.

excerpt: Overall, our decision to prioritize the capabilities in the two tables above is based on commissioned research reports, discussions with domain experts, input from expert forecasters, public research, conversations with other industry actors through the Frontier Model Forum, and internal discussions.
paraphrase: The prioritized capabilities were selected based on research, expert discussions, forecaster input, public research, industry conversations via the Frontier Model Forum, and internal deliberation.

excerpt: As the field evolves and our understanding deepens, we remain committed to refining our approach.
paraphrase: Anthropic commits to continuing to refine its approach as the field and understanding evolve.

excerpt: We recognize the potential risks of highly persuasive AI models. While we are actively consulting experts, we believe this capability is not yet sufficiently understood to include in our current commitments.
paraphrase: Anthropic acknowledges persuasive AI risks but considers the capability not yet sufficiently understood to warrant inclusion in current commitments.

excerpt: We will routinely test models to determine whether their capabilities fall sufficiently far below the Capability Thresholds such that we are confident that the ASL-2 Standard remains appropriate.
paraphrase: Routine testing will confirm that models remain sufficiently below Capability Thresholds so ASL-2 remains appropriate.

excerpt: We will first conduct preliminary assessments (on both new and existing models, as needed) to determine whether a more comprehensive evaluation is needed.
paraphrase: Preliminary assessments will be conducted on new and existing models as needed to determine whether comprehensive evaluation is required.

excerpt: The purpose of this preliminary assessment is to identify whether the model is notably more capable than the last model that underwent a comprehensive assessment.
paraphrase: The preliminary assessment aims to determine whether a model is notably more capable than the last comprehensively assessed model.

excerpt: The term "notably more capable" is operationalized as at least one of the following:
paraphrase: The term "notably more capable" is defined by at least one of the listed conditions.

context_stem: The term "notably more capable" is operationalized as at least one of the following:
excerpt: The model is notably more performant on automated tests in risk-relevant domains (defined as 4x or more in Effective Compute).
paraphrase: One trigger for "notably more capable" is at least a 4x increase in Effective Compute-equivalent performance on risk-relevant automated tests.

context_stem: The term "notably more capable" is operationalized as at least one of the following:
excerpt: Six months' worth of finetuning and other capability elicitation methods have accumulated. This is measured in calendar time, since we do not yet have a metric to estimate the impact of these improvements more precisely.
paraphrase: The second trigger is six months of accumulated finetuning and elicitation methods, measured in calendar time absent a more precise metric.

excerpt: In addition, the Responsible Scaling Officer may in their discretion determine that a comprehensive assessment is warranted.
paraphrase: The Responsible Scaling Officer has discretion to determine that comprehensive assessment is warranted regardless of the standard criteria.

excerpt: If a new or existing model is below the "notably more capable" standard, no further testing is necessary.
paraphrase: No further testing is required if a model falls below the "notably more capable" standard.

excerpt: For models requiring comprehensive testing, we will assess whether the model is unlikely to reach any relevant Capability Thresholds absent surprising advances in widely accessible post-training enhancements.
paraphrase: Comprehensive testing assesses whether a model is unlikely to reach relevant Capability Thresholds barring unexpected accessible post-training advances.

excerpt: To make the required showing, we will need to satisfy the following criteria:
paraphrase: Satisfying the required showing requires meeting the following listed criteria.

context_stem: To make the required showing, we will need to satisfy the following criteria:
excerpt: Threat model mapping: For each capability threshold, make a compelling case that we have mapped out the most likely and consequential threat models: combinations of actors (if relevant), attack pathways, model capability bottlenecks, and types of harms.
paraphrase: Criterion one requires mapping out the most likely and consequential threat models, including actors, attack pathways, capability bottlenecks, and harm types.

excerpt: We also make a compelling case that there does not exist a threat model that we are not evaluating that represents a substantial amount of risk.
paraphrase: Criterion one also requires demonstrating that no unevaluated threat model represents substantial risk.

context_stem: To make the required showing, we will need to satisfy the following criteria:
excerpt: Evaluations: Design and run empirical tests that provide strong evidence that the model does not have the requisite skills; explain why the tests yielded such results; and check at test time that the results are attributable to the model's capabilities rather than issues with the test design.
paraphrase: Criterion two requires empirical tests demonstrating the model lacks requisite skills, with explanation of results and verification that they reflect model capability rather than test design flaws.

excerpt: Findings from partner organizations and external evaluations of our models (or similar models) should also be incorporated into the final assessment, when available.
paraphrase: Findings from partner organizations and external evaluations should be incorporated into the final assessment when available.

context_stem: To make the required showing, we will need to satisfy the following criteria:
excerpt: Elicitation: Demonstrate that, when given enough resources to extrapolate to realistic attackers, researchers cannot elicit sufficiently useful results from the model on the relevant tasks.
paraphrase: Criterion three requires demonstrating that researchers, given realistic attacker-level resources, cannot elicit sufficiently useful results from the model.

excerpt: We should assume that jailbreaks and model weight theft are possibilities, and therefore perform testing on models without safety mechanisms (such as harmlessness training) that could obscure these capabilities.
paraphrase: Testing should assume jailbreaks and weight theft are possible and be conducted on models without safety mechanisms that might mask true capabilities.

excerpt: We will also consider the possible performance increase from using resources that a realistic attacker would have access to, such as scaffolding, finetuning, and expert prompting.
paraphrase: Consideration will be given to performance gains from resources realistic attackers could access, such as scaffolding, finetuning, and expert prompting.

excerpt: At minimum, we will perform basic finetuning for instruction following, tool use, minimizing refusal rates.
paraphrase: At a minimum, basic finetuning will be performed for instruction following, tool use, and reduced refusal rates.

excerpt: "Effective Compute" is a scaling-trend-based metric that accounts for both FLOPs and algorithmic improvements. An Effective Compute increase of K represents a performance improvement from a pretrained model on relevant task(s) equivalent to scaling up the baseline model's training compute by a factor of K.
paraphrase: Effective Compute is defined as a metric combining FLOPs and algorithmic improvements, where an increase of K equals a performance gain equivalent to scaling training compute by factor K.

excerpt: We plan to track Effective Compute during pretraining on a weighted aggregation of datasets relevant to our Capability Thresholds (e.g., coding and science).
paraphrase: Effective Compute will be tracked during pretraining using a weighted aggregation of relevant datasets like coding and science.

excerpt: This is, however, an open research question, and we will explore different possible methods.
paraphrase: Anthropic acknowledges this is an open research question and will explore different methods.

excerpt: More generally, the Effective Compute concept is fairly new, and we may replace it with another metric in a similar spirit in the future.
paraphrase: The Effective Compute concept is new and may be replaced by a similar future metric.

excerpt: This is a broad category, including techniques like improved prompting and agent scaffolding.
paraphrase: The category of capability elicitation methods is broad, including improved prompting and agent scaffolding.

excerpt: Exploring ways to integrate these types of improvements into an overall metric is an ongoing area of research.
paraphrase: Integrating these improvements into an overall metric remains an ongoing research area.

excerpt: By "widely accessible," we mean techniques that are available to a moderately resourced group (i.e., do not involve setting up large amounts of custom infrastructure or using confidential information).
paraphrase: "Widely accessible" is defined as techniques available to a moderately resourced group without large custom infrastructure or confidential information.

excerpt: We include headroom to account for the possibility that the model is either modified via one of our own finetuning products or stolen in the months following testing, and used to create a model that has reached a Capability Threshold.
paraphrase: Headroom is built in to account for possible finetuning or theft after testing that could push a model to a Capability Threshold.

excerpt: That said, estimating these future effects is very difficult given the state of research today.
paraphrase: Estimating these future effects is acknowledged as very difficult given current research limitations.

context_stem: To make the required showing, we will need to satisfy the following criteria:
excerpt: Forecasting: Make informal forecasts about the likelihood that further training and elicitation will improve test results between the time of testing and the next expected round of comprehensive testing.
paraphrase: Criterion four requires informal forecasts of the likelihood that further training and elicitation will improve results before the next comprehensive testing round.

excerpt: This testing and the subsequent capability decision should ideally be concluded within about a month of reaching the "notably more capable" threshold.
paraphrase: Testing and the resulting capability decision should ideally conclude within about a month of reaching the "notably more capable" threshold.

excerpt: If, after the comprehensive testing, we determine that the model is sufficiently below the relevant Capability Thresholds, then we will continue to apply the ASL-2 Standard.
paraphrase: ASL-2 continues to apply if comprehensive testing shows the model is sufficiently below relevant thresholds.

excerpt: The process for making such a determination is as follows:
paraphrase: The following steps describe the determination process.

context_stem: The process for making such a determination is as follows:
excerpt: First, we will compile a Capability Report that documents the findings from the comprehensive assessment, makes an affirmative case for why the Capability Threshold is sufficiently far away, and advances recommendations on deployment decisions.
paraphrase: Step one requires compiling a Capability Report documenting findings, an affirmative case for distance from the threshold, and deployment recommendations.

context_stem: The process for making such a determination is as follows:
excerpt: The report will be escalated to the CEO and the Responsible Scaling Officer, who will (1) make the ultimate determination as to whether we have sufficiently established that we are unlikely to reach the Capability Threshold and (2) decide any deployment-related issues.
paraphrase: Step two escalates the report to the CEO and RSO, who make the final determination on threshold proximity and deployment issues.

context_stem: The process for making such a determination is as follows:
excerpt: In general, as noted in Sections 7.1.4 and 7.2.2, we will solicit both internal and external expert feedback on the report as well as the CEO and RSO's conclusions to inform future refinements to our methodology.
paraphrase: Step three involves generally soliciting internal and external expert feedback on the report and conclusions to inform future methodology.

excerpt: For high-stakes issues, however, the CEO and RSO will likely solicit internal and external feedback on the report prior to making any decisions.
paraphrase: For high-stakes issues, the CEO and RSO will likely solicit feedback before making decisions, rather than after.

context_stem: The process for making such a determination is as follows:
excerpt: If the CEO and RSO decide to proceed with deployment, they will share their decision–as well as the underlying Capability Report, internal feedback, and any external feedback–with the Board of Directors and the Long-Term Benefit Trust before moving forward.
paraphrase: Step four requires sharing the deployment decision and supporting materials with the Board of Directors and the Long-Term Benefit Trust before proceeding.

excerpt: If, however, we determine we are unable to make the required showing, we will act as though the model has surpassed the Capability Threshold.
paraphrase: If the required showing cannot be made, the model will be treated as having surpassed the Capability Threshold.

excerpt: This means that we will (1) upgrade to the ASL-3 Required Safeguards (see Section 4) and (2) conduct follow-up a capability assessment to confirm that the ASL-4 Standard is not necessary (see Section 5).
paraphrase: This triggers upgrading to ASL-3 Required Safeguards and conducting a follow-up assessment to confirm ASL-4 is unnecessary.

excerpt: To determine whether the measures we have adopted satisfy the ASL-3 Required Safeguards, we will conduct a safeguards assessment.
paraphrase: Anthropic will conduct a safeguards assessment to determine whether adopted measures satisfy the ASL-3 Required Safeguards.

excerpt: As noted, the Required Safeguards for each Capability Threshold are specified in Section 2.
paraphrase: The Required Safeguards for each Capability Threshold are specified elsewhere in Section 2.

excerpt: We will document our implementation of the Required Safeguards in a Safeguards Report.
paraphrase: Anthropic will document its implementation of the Required Safeguards in a Safeguards Report.

excerpt: Currently, these will be informal estimates of (1) the extent to which widely available elicitation techniques may improve and (2) how the model will perform on the same tasks when the next round of testing begins.
paraphrase: The footnote explains that these forecasts are currently informal estimates about elicitation technique improvement and future model performance.

excerpt: As these are open research questions, we will aim to improve these forecasts over time so that they can be relied upon for risk judgments.
paraphrase: Because these are open research questions, Anthropic aims to improve the forecasts over time for reliable risk judgments.

excerpt: In the case where the capability assessment shows a model is just barely below the threshold, the Responsible Scaling Officer may choose to limit further training to some amount less than the default 4x Effective Compute increase until ASL-3 measures are in place, in order to limit risk.
paraphrase: If a model is just barely below the threshold, the Responsible Scaling Officer may restrict further training below the default 4x Effective Compute increase until ASL-3 measures are implemented.

excerpt: There may be a substantial period during which models are not demonstrably close to the Capability Threshold, but we nevertheless are unable to rule out the risk to our satisfaction, and thus choose to implement the Required Safeguards.
paraphrase: Even when models aren't clearly close to the Capability Threshold, Anthropic may still implement Required Safeguards if risk cannot be ruled out to its satisfaction.

excerpt: When a model must meet the ASL-3 Deployment Standard, we will evaluate whether the measures we have implemented make us robust to persistent attempts to misuse the capability in question.
paraphrase: When the ASL-3 Deployment Standard applies, Anthropic will assess whether its measures make it robust against persistent misuse attempts.

excerpt: To make the required showing, we will need to satisfy the following criteria:
paraphrase: Anthropic states it must satisfy the following listed criteria to make the required showing.

context_stem: To make the required showing, we will need to satisfy the following criteria:
excerpt: Threat modeling: Make a compelling case that the set of threats and the vectors through which an adversary could catastrophically misuse the deployed system have been sufficiently mapped out, and will commit to revising as necessary over time.
paraphrase: Anthropic must show that threats and misuse vectors have been adequately mapped and commit to revising this over time.

context_stem: To make the required showing, we will need to satisfy the following criteria:
excerpt: Defense in depth: Use a "defense in depth" approach by building a series of defensive layers, each designed to catch misuse attempts that might pass through previous barriers.
paraphrase: Anthropic must build layered defenses that catch misuse attempts that slip past earlier layers.

excerpt: As an example, this might entail achieving a high overall recall rate using harm refusal techniques. This is an area of active research, and new technologies may be added when ready.
paraphrase: An example is achieving high recall via harm refusal techniques; this remains an active research area where new technologies may be added.

context_stem: To make the required showing, we will need to satisfy the following criteria:
excerpt: Red-teaming: Conduct red-teaming that demonstrates that threat actors with realistic access levels and resources are highly unlikely to be able to consistently elicit information from any generally accessible systems that greatly increases their ability to cause catastrophic harm relative to other available tools.
paraphrase: Anthropic must conduct red-teaming demonstrating that realistic threat actors are highly unlikely to consistently extract catastrophic-harm-enabling information beyond what other tools provide.

context_stem: To make the required showing, we will need to satisfy the following criteria:
excerpt: Rapid remediation: Show that any compromises of the deployed system, such as jailbreaks or other attack pathways, will be identified and remediated promptly enough to prevent the overall system from meaningfully increasing an adversary's ability to cause catastrophic harm.
paraphrase: Anthropic must demonstrate that system compromises will be identified and fixed quickly enough to prevent meaningful increases in catastrophic harm capability.

excerpt: Example techniques could include rapid vulnerability patching, the ability to escalate to law enforcement when appropriate, and any necessary retention of logs for these activities.
paraphrase: Examples include rapid patching, escalation to law enforcement, and log retention.

context_stem: To make the required showing, we will need to satisfy the following criteria:
excerpt: Monitoring: Prespecify empirical evidence that would show the system is operating within the accepted risk range and define a process for reviewing the system's performance on a reasonable cadence.
paraphrase: Anthropic must prespecify evidence showing the system operates within accepted risk range and define a regular review process.

excerpt: Process examples include monitoring responses to jailbreak bounties, doing historical analysis or background monitoring, and any necessary retention of logs for these activities.
paraphrase: Examples include monitoring jailbreak bounty responses, historical/background analysis, and log retention.

context_stem: To make the required showing, we will need to satisfy the following criteria:
excerpt: Trusted users: Establish criteria for determining when it may be appropriate to share a version of the model with reduced safeguards with trusted users.
paraphrase: Anthropic must set criteria for when sharing a reduced-safeguard model version with trusted users is appropriate.

excerpt: In addition, demonstrate that an alternative set of controls will provide equivalent levels of assurance. This could include a sufficient combination of user vetting, secure access controls, monitoring, log retention, and incident response protocols.
paraphrase: Anthropic must also show that alternative controls provide equivalent assurance, potentially combining vetting, access controls, monitoring, log retention, and incident response.

context_stem: To make the required showing, we will need to satisfy the following criteria:
excerpt: Third-party environments: Document how all relevant models will meet the criteria above, even if they are deployed in a third-party partner's environment that may have a different set of safeguards.
paraphrase: Anthropic must document how models meet these criteria even when deployed in third-party environments with different safeguards.

excerpt: When a model must meet the ASL-3 Security Standard, we will evaluate whether the measures we have implemented make us highly protected against most attackers' attempts at stealing model weights.
paraphrase: When the ASL-3 Security Standard applies, Anthropic will assess whether its measures provide strong protection against most weight-theft attempts.

excerpt: This criterion does not attempt to specify the exact red-teaming protocol (e.g., number of hours, level of access, or pass-fail criteria). Setting a principled pass-fail threshold will depend on other factors, such as the quality of our monitoring and ability to respond to jailbreaks rapidly.
paraphrase: The footnote clarifies that the red-teaming criterion does not fix a specific protocol, since a principled threshold depends on other factors like monitoring quality and response speed.

excerpt: Due to the likely ease of bypassing or removing safeguards via fine-tuning, it may be difficult or impossible for these red-teaming tests to pass if weights are released or if unmoderated fine-tuning access is provided to untrusted users.
paraphrase: The footnote notes that red-teaming tests may be difficult or impossible to pass if weights are released or unmoderated fine-tuning access is given to untrusted users, due to easy safeguard bypass via fine-tuning.

excerpt: We consider the following groups in scope: hacktivists, criminal hacker groups, organized cybercrime groups, terrorist organizations, corporate espionage teams, internal employees, and state-sponsored programs that use broad-based and non-targeted techniques (i.e., not novel attack chains).
paraphrase: Anthropic defines the in-scope threat actor groups for the ASL-3 Security Standard, including hacktivists, criminal groups, terrorists, insiders, and state actors using non-targeted techniques.

excerpt: The following groups are out of scope for the ASL-3 Security Standard because further testing (as discussed below) should confirm that the model would not meaningfully increase their ability to do harm: state-sponsored programs that specifically target us (e.g., through novel attack chains or insider compromise) and a small number (~10) of non-state actors with state-level resourcing or backing that are capable of developing novel attack chains that utilize 0-day attacks.
paraphrase: Certain highly sophisticated actors, including targeted state programs and about ten non-state actors with state-level resources, are excluded from ASL-3 Security Standard scope since further testing should confirm no meaningful harm increase.

excerpt: To make the required showing, we will need to satisfy the following criteria:
paraphrase: Anthropic states it must satisfy the following listed criteria to make the required showing for the Security Standard.

context_stem: To make the required showing, we will need to satisfy the following criteria:
excerpt: Threat modeling: Follow risk governance best practices, such as use of the MITRE ATT&CK Framework to establish the relationship between the identified threats, sensitive assets, attack vectors and, in doing so, sufficiently capture the resulting risks that must be addressed to protect model weights from theft attempts.
paraphrase: Anthropic must follow risk governance best practices, such as MITRE ATT&CK, to map threats, assets, and vectors and capture resulting weight-theft risks.

excerpt: As part of this requirement, we should specify our plans for revising the resulting threat model over time.
paraphrase: Anthropic should specify plans for revising the threat model over time.

context_stem: To make the required showing, we will need to satisfy the following criteria:
excerpt: Security frameworks: Align to and, as needed, extend industry-standard security frameworks for addressing identified risks, such as disclosure of sensitive information, tampering with accounts and assets, and unauthorized elevation of privileges with the appropriate controls.
paraphrase: Anthropic must align with, and extend as needed, industry-standard security frameworks to address risks like data disclosure, tampering, and privilege escalation.

excerpt: Perimeters and access controls: Building strong perimeters and access controls around sensitive assets to ensure AI models and critical systems are protected from unauthorized access.
paraphrase: Anthropic must build strong perimeters and access controls to protect models and critical systems from unauthorized access.

excerpt: We expect this will include a combination of physical security, encryption, cloud security, infrastructure policy, access management, and weight access minimization and monitoring.
paraphrase: Anthropic expects this to combine physical security, encryption, cloud security, infrastructure policy, access management, and weight access minimization/monitoring.

excerpt: Lifecycle security: Securing links in the chain of systems and software used to develop models, to prevent compromised components from being introduced and to ensure only trusted code and hardware is used.
paraphrase: Anthropic must secure the development chain to prevent compromised components and ensure only trusted code and hardware are used.

excerpt: We expect this will include a combination of software inventory, supply chain security, artifact integrity, binary authorization, hardware procurement, and secure research development lifecycle.
paraphrase: Anthropic expects this to combine software inventory, supply chain security, artifact integrity, binary authorization, hardware procurement, and secure R&D lifecycle practices.

excerpt: Monitoring: Proactively identifying and mitigating threats through ongoing and effective monitoring, testing for vulnerabilities, and laying traps for potential attackers.
paraphrase: Anthropic must proactively identify and mitigate threats via ongoing monitoring, vulnerability testing, and attacker traps.

excerpt: We expect this will include a combination of endpoint patching, product security testing, log management, asset monitoring, and intruder deception techniques.
paraphrase: Anthropic expects this to combine endpoint patching, product security testing, log management, asset monitoring, and deception techniques.

excerpt: Resourcing: Investing sufficient resources in security.
paraphrase: Anthropic must invest sufficient resources in security.

excerpt: We expect meeting this standard of security to require roughly 5-10% of employees being dedicated to security and security-adjacent work.
paraphrase: Anthropic expects that meeting this security standard requires roughly 5-10% of employees dedicated to security-related work.

excerpt: Existing guidance: Aligning where appropriate with existing guidance on securing model weights, including Securing AI Model Weights, Preventing Theft and Misuse of Frontier Models (2024); security recommendations like Deploying AI Systems Securely (CISA/NSA/FBI/ASD/CCCS/GCSB/GCHQ), ISO 42001, CSA's AI Safety Initiative, and CoSAI; and standards frameworks like SSDF, SOC 2, NIST 800-53.
paraphrase: Anthropic will align where appropriate with existing guidance and standards such as Securing AI Model Weights, Deploying AI Systems Securely, ISO 42001, CoSAI, SSDF, SOC 2, and NIST 800-53.

excerpt: We will implement robust controls to mitigate basic insider risk, but consider mitigating risks from sophisticated or state-compromised insiders to be out of scope for ASL-3.
paraphrase: Anthropic will implement robust controls for basic insider risk but excludes sophisticated or state-compromised insider risk from ASL-3 scope.

excerpt: We define "basic insider risk" as risk from an insider who does not have persistent or time-limited access to systems that process model weights.
paraphrase: The footnote defines basic insider risk as risk from an insider lacking persistent or time-limited access to weight-processing systems.

excerpt: We define "sophisticated insider risk" as risk from an insider who has persistent access or can request time-limited access to systems that process model weights.
paraphrase: The footnote defines sophisticated insider risk as risk from an insider with persistent or requestable time-limited access to weight-processing systems.

excerpt: We are committed to further enhancing these protections as a part of our ongoing preparations for higher security levels.
paraphrase: Anthropic commits to further enhancing insider risk protections as part of preparing for higher security levels.

context_stem: To make the required showing, we will need to satisfy the following criteria:
excerpt: Audits: Develop plans to (1) audit and assess the design and implementation of the security program and (2) share these findings (and updates on any remediation efforts) with management on an appropriate cadence.
paraphrase: Anthropic must develop plans to audit the security program and share findings and remediation updates with management regularly.

excerpt: We expect this to include independent validation of threat modeling and risk assessment results; a sampling-based audit of the operating effectiveness of the defined controls; periodic, broadly scoped, and independent testing with expert red-teamers who are industry-renowned and have been recognized in competitive challenges.
paraphrase: Anthropic expects audits to include independent validation of threat modeling and risk assessments, sampling-based control audits, and periodic independent testing by renowned expert red-teamers.

context_stem: To make the required showing, we will need to satisfy the following criteria:
excerpt: Third-party environments: Document how all relevant models will meet the criteria above, even if they are deployed in a third-party partner's environment that may have a different set of safeguards.
paraphrase: Anthropic must document how models meet security criteria even when deployed in third-party partner environments with different safeguards.

excerpt: If, after the evaluations above, we determine that we have met the ASL-3 Required Safeguards, then we may proceed with deploying and training models above the Capability Threshold, provided we have also conducted a follow-up capability assessment.
paraphrase: If Anthropic determines it has met the ASL-3 Required Safeguards, it may proceed with deployment and training above the Capability Threshold, contingent on a follow-up capability assessment.

excerpt: The process for determining whether we have met the ASL-3 Required Safeguards is as follows:
paraphrase: The following steps describe the process for determining whether ASL-3 Required Safeguards have been met.

context_stem: The process for determining whether we have met the ASL-3 Required Safeguards is as follows:
excerpt: First, we will compile a Safeguards Report for each Required Safeguard that documents our implementation of the measures above, makes an affirmative case for why we have satisfied them, and advances recommendations on deployment decisions.
paraphrase: Anthropic will first compile a Safeguards Report per Required Safeguard documenting implementation, arguing satisfaction, and recommending deployment decisions.

context_stem: The process for determining whether we have met the ASL-3 Required Safeguards is as follows:
excerpt: The Safeguards Report(s) will be escalated to the CEO and the Responsible Scaling Officer, who will (1) make the ultimate determination as to whether we have satisfied the Required Safeguards and (2) decide any deployment-related issues.
paraphrase: The Safeguards Report will go to the CEO and RSO, who will make the final determination on Required Safeguards satisfaction and decide deployment issues.

context_stem: The process for determining whether we have met the ASL-3 Required Safeguards is as follows:
excerpt: In general, as noted in Sections 7.1.4 and 7.2.2, we will solicit both internal and external expert feedback on the report as well as the CEO and RSO's conclusions to inform future refinements to our methodology.
paraphrase: Anthropic will generally solicit internal and external expert feedback on the report and the CEO/RSO conclusions to refine future methodology.

excerpt: For high-stakes issues, however, the CEO and RSO will likely solicit internal and external feedback on the report prior to making any decisions.
paraphrase: For high-stakes issues, the CEO and RSO will likely seek internal and external feedback before deciding.

context_stem: The process for determining whether we have met the ASL-3 Required Safeguards is as follows:
excerpt: If the CEO and RSO decide to proceed with deployment and training, they will share their decision–as well as the underlying Safeguards Report, internal feedback, and any external feedback–with the Board of Directors and the Long-Term Benefit Trust before moving forward.
paraphrase: If the CEO and RSO decide to proceed, they will share the decision, Safeguards Report, and feedback with the Board and Long-Term Benefit Trust before proceeding.

context_stem: The process for determining whether we have met the ASL-3 Required Safeguards is as follows:
excerpt: After the ASL-3 Required Safeguards are approved, they will be revisited and re-approved at least annually to re-affirm their suitability and sound implementation.
paraphrase: Once approved, ASL-3 Required Safeguards will be reviewed and re-approved at least once a year.

excerpt: If, however, we are unable to make the showing required above, we will restrict model deployment and further scaling.
paraphrase: If Anthropic cannot make the required showing, it will restrict deployment and further scaling of the model.

excerpt: In parallel with upgrading a model to the Required Safeguards, we will (1) update this policy to include any additional Capability Thresholds for which the Required Safeguards would be insufficient; and (2) conduct a follow-up capability assessment to determine that the model's capabilities fall sufficiently far away from those Capability Thresholds, following the procedures outlined in Section 3.
paraphrase: While upgrading a model's safeguards, Anthropic will update the policy for any new insufficient thresholds and conduct a follow-up capability assessment following Section 3 procedures.

excerpt: To summarize the commitments and procedures outlined above, we may deploy or store a model if either of the following criteria are met: (1) the model's capabilities are sufficiently far away from the existing Capability Thresholds, making the current ASL-2 Standard appropriate;
paraphrase: Anthropic may deploy or store a model if its capabilities are sufficiently far from existing Capability Thresholds, keeping ASL-2 appropriate.

excerpt: or (2) the model's capabilities have surpassed the existing Capabilities Threshold, but we have implemented the ASL-3 Required Safeguards and confirmed that the model is sufficiently far away from the next set of Capability Thresholds as to make the model ASL-3 Standard appropriate.
paraphrase: Or the model may be deployed if it has surpassed the existing threshold but ASL-3 Required Safeguards are implemented and confirmed sufficient relative to the next threshold set.

excerpt: We may also continue to train more capable models, conducting preliminary and comprehensive assessments as before.
paraphrase: Anthropic may continue training more capable models while conducting preliminary and comprehensive assessments as before.

excerpt: In any scenario where we determine that a model requires ASL-3 Required Safeguards but we are unable to implement them immediately, we will act promptly to reduce interim risk to acceptable levels until the ASL-3 Required Safeguards are in place:
paraphrase: If a model requires ASL-3 Required Safeguards that cannot be implemented immediately, Anthropic will act promptly to reduce interim risk to acceptable levels until safeguards are in place.

excerpt: Interim measures: The CEO and Responsible Scaling Officer may approve the use of interim measures that provide the same level of assurance as the relevant ASL-3 Standard but are faster or simpler to implement.
paraphrase: The CEO and RSO may approve interim measures providing equivalent assurance to the ASL-3 Standard but quicker or simpler to implement.

excerpt: In the deployment context, such measures might include blocking model responses, downgrading to a less-capable model in a particular domain, or increasing the sensitivity of automated monitoring.
paraphrase: Deployment-context interim measures might include blocking responses, downgrading to a less-capable model, or increasing monitoring sensitivity.

excerpt: In the security context, an example of such a measure would be storing the model weights in a single-purpose, isolated network that meets the ASL-3 Standard.
paraphrase: A security-context interim measure example is storing model weights in an isolated, single-purpose network meeting the ASL-3 Standard.

excerpt: In either case, the CEO and Responsible Scaling Officer will share their plan with the Board of Directors and the Long-Term Benefit Trust.
paraphrase: In either context, the CEO and RSO will share their interim measures plan with the Board and Long-Term Benefit Trust.

excerpt: Stronger restrictions: In the unlikely event that we cannot implement interim measures to adequately mitigate risk, we will impose stronger restrictions.
paraphrase: If interim measures cannot adequately mitigate risk, Anthropic will impose stronger restrictions.

excerpt: In the deployment context, we will de-deploy the model and replace it with a model that falls below the Capability Threshold. Once the ASL-3 Deployment Standard can be met, the model may be re-deployed.
paraphrase: In deployment, Anthropic will de-deploy the model and replace it with one below the Capability Threshold, allowing re-deployment once the ASL-3 Deployment Standard is met.

excerpt: In the security context, we will delete model weights. Given the availability of interim deployment and security protections, however, stronger restrictions should rarely be necessary.
paraphrase: In the security context, Anthropic will delete model weights, though stronger restrictions should rarely be needed given interim protections.

excerpt: Monitoring pretraining: We will not train models with comparable or greater capabilities to the one that requires the ASL-3 Security Standard.
paraphrase: Anthropic will not train models with capabilities comparable to or greater than one requiring the ASL-3 Security Standard.

excerpt: This is achieved by monitoring the capabilities of the model in pretraining and comparing them against the given model.
paraphrase: This is done by monitoring pretraining model capabilities and comparing them to the given model.

excerpt: If the pretraining model's capabilities are comparable or greater, we will pause training until we have implemented the ASL-3 Security Standard and established it is sufficient for the model.
paraphrase: If the pretraining model's capabilities are comparable or greater, Anthropic will pause training until the ASL-3 Security Standard is implemented and confirmed sufficient.

excerpt: We will set expectations with internal stakeholders about the potential for such pauses.
paraphrase: Anthropic will set expectations with internal stakeholders regarding the possibility of such training pauses.

excerpt: When choosing amongst options that satisfy the safety criteria, we will implement whichever interim safeguards minimize changes to customer experience.
paraphrase: Among safety-compliant options, Anthropic will implement whichever interim safeguards minimize customer experience changes.

excerpt: We consider implementation of the ASL-3 Security Standard alone sufficient to continue training, regardless of whether the ASL-3 Deployment Standard is satisfied.
paraphrase: The footnote states that implementing only the ASL-3 Security Standard suffices to continue training, regardless of the Deployment Standard's status.

excerpt: "Comparable or greater capabilities" is operationalized as 1x or more in Effective Compute.
paraphrase: The footnote defines "comparable or greater capabilities" as 1x or more Effective Compute.

context_stem: To facilitate the effective implementation of this policy across the company, we commit to the following:
excerpt: Responsible Scaling Officer: We will maintain the position of Responsible Scaling Officer, a designated member of staff who is responsible for reducing catastrophic risk, primarily by ensuring this policy is designed and implemented effectively.
paraphrase: Anthropic commits to maintaining a Responsible Scaling Officer role responsible for reducing catastrophic risk through effective policy design and implementation.

excerpt: The Responsible Scaling Officer's duties will include (but are not limited to): (1) as needed, proposing updates to this policy to the Board of Directors; (2) approving relevant model training or deployment decisions based on capability and safeguard assessments;
paraphrase: The RSO's duties include proposing policy updates and approving training/deployment decisions based on assessments.

excerpt: (3) reviewing major contracts (i.e., deployment partnerships) for consistency with this policy; (4) overseeing implementation of this policy, including the allocation of sufficient resources; (5) receiving and addressing reports of potential instances of noncompliance;
paraphrase: The RSO's duties also include reviewing major contracts, overseeing implementation and resource allocation, and handling noncompliance reports.

excerpt: (6) promptly notifying the Board of Directors of any cases of noncompliance that pose material risk; and (7) making judgment calls on policy interpretation and application.
paraphrase: The RSO's final duties are notifying the Board of material noncompliance and making interpretive judgment calls.

excerpt: Readiness: We will develop internal safety procedures for incident scenarios. Such scenarios include (1) pausing training in response to reaching Capability Thresholds; (2) responding to a security incident involving model weights; and (3) responding to severe jailbreaks or vulnerabilities in deployed models, including restricting access in safety emergencies that cannot otherwise be mitigated.
paraphrase: Anthropic will develop internal procedures covering incident scenarios such as training pauses, security incidents, and severe jailbreaks.

excerpt: We will run exercises to ensure our readiness for incident scenarios.
paraphrase: Anthropic will conduct exercises to test readiness for incident scenarios.

excerpt: Transparency: We will share summaries of Capability Reports and Safeguards Reports with Anthropic's regular-clearance staff, redacting any highly-sensitive information.
paraphrase: Anthropic will share redacted report summaries with regular-clearance staff.

excerpt: We will share a minimally redacted version of these reports with a subset of staff, to help us surface relevant technical safety considerations.
paraphrase: A minimally redacted version of the reports will go to a subset of staff to surface technical safety issues.

excerpt: Internal review: For each Capabilities or Safeguards Report, we will solicit feedback from internal teams with visibility into the relevant activities, with the aims of informing future refinements to our methodology and, in some circumstances, identifying weaknesses and informing the CEO and RSO's decisions.
paraphrase: For each report, Anthropic will solicit internal team feedback to refine methodology and inform leadership decisions.

excerpt: Noncompliance: We will maintain a process through which Anthropic staff may anonymously notify the Responsible Scaling Officer of any potential instances of noncompliance with this policy.
paraphrase: Anthropic will maintain an anonymous reporting process for noncompliance to the RSO.

excerpt: We will also establish a policy governing noncompliance reporting, which will (1) protect reporters from retaliation and (2) set forth a mechanism for escalating reports to one or more members of the Board of Directors in cases where the report relates to conduct of the Responsible Scaling Officer.
paraphrase: Anthropic will establish a reporting policy that protects reporters and provides escalation to the Board for reports about the RSO.

excerpt: Further, we will track and investigate any reported or otherwise identified potential instances of noncompliance with this policy.
paraphrase: Anthropic will track and investigate all identified noncompliance instances.

excerpt: Where reports are substantiated, we will take appropriate and proportional corrective action and document the same.
paraphrase: Substantiated reports will result in proportional corrective action, documented accordingly.

excerpt: The Responsible Scaling Officer will regularly update the Board of Directors on substantial cases of noncompliance and overall trends.
paraphrase: The RSO will regularly brief the Board on major noncompliance cases and trends.

excerpt: In addition to noncompliance processes, we will (1) establish pathways for Anthropic staff to raise any issues related to this policy, including the overall risk levels of our models and implementation challenges; and (2) regularly review our compliance with this policy's procedural requirements.
paraphrase: Beyond noncompliance channels, Anthropic will create issue-raising pathways and conduct regular compliance reviews.

excerpt: Cases deemed to present minimal additional risk may be reported to the Board in quarterly summary reports.
paraphrase: Low-risk cases can be reported to the Board via quarterly summaries instead of individually.

excerpt: In cases where this policy is unintentionally ambiguous, we will act in accordance with the Responsible Scaling Officer or CEO's judgment, and aim to clarify the ambiguity in the next policy update.
paraphrase: Ambiguities will be resolved via RSO or CEO judgment, with clarification intended in a subsequent update.

excerpt: Employee agreements: We will not impose contractual non-disparagement obligations on employees, candidates, or former employees in a way that could impede or discourage them from publicly raising safety concerns about Anthropic.
paraphrase: Anthropic will not use non-disparagement clauses to discourage employees from raising safety concerns.

excerpt: If we offer agreements with a non-disparagement clause, that clause will not preclude raising safety concerns, nor will it preclude disclosure of the existence of that clause.
paraphrase: Any non-disparagement clause offered will not block safety-concern disclosure or disclosure of the clause itself.

excerpt: Policy changes: Changes to this policy will be proposed by the CEO and the Responsible Scaling Officer and approved by the Board of Directors, in consultation with the Long-Term Benefit Trust.
paraphrase: Policy changes are proposed by the CEO and RSO and approved by the Board with LTBT consultation.

excerpt: The current version of the RSP is accessible at www.anthropic.com/rsp. We will update the public version of the RSP before any changes take effect and record any differences from the prior draft in a change log.
paraphrase: The current RSP is published online, and any changes will be publicly updated before taking effect with differences logged.

context_stem: To advance the public dialogue on the regulation of frontier AI model risks and to enable examination of our actions, we commit to the following:
excerpt: Public disclosures: We will publicly release key information related to the evaluation and deployment of our models (not including sensitive details). These include summaries of related Capability and Safeguards reports when we deploy a model as well as plans for current and future comprehensive capability assessments and deployment and security safeguards.
paraphrase: Anthropic will publicly release non-sensitive information including report summaries at deployment and plans for capability assessments and safeguards.

excerpt: We will also periodically release information on internal reports of potential instances of non-compliance and other implementation challenges we encounter.
paraphrase: Anthropic will periodically release information about internal noncompliance reports and implementation challenges.

excerpt: Expert input: We will solicit input from external experts in relevant domains in the process of developing and conducting capability and safeguards assessments.
paraphrase: Anthropic will solicit external expert input during development and conduct of capability and safeguards assessments.

excerpt: We may also solicit external expert input prior to making final decisions on the capability and safeguards assessments.
paraphrase: Anthropic may also seek external expert input before finalizing assessment decisions.

excerpt: U.S. Government notice: We will notify a relevant U.S. Government entity if a model requires stronger protections than the ASL-2 Standard.
paraphrase: Anthropic will notify a relevant U.S. Government entity if a model needs protections beyond ASL-2.

excerpt: Procedural compliance review: On approximately an annual basis, we will commission a third-party review that assesses whether we adhered to this policy's main procedural commitments (we expect to iterate on the exact list since this has not been done before for RSPs).
paraphrase: Anthropic will commission an annual third-party review of adherence to procedural commitments, expecting to refine the review's scope over time.

excerpt: This review will focus on procedural compliance, not substantive outcomes. We will also do such reviews internally on a more regular cadence.
paraphrase: The third-party review focuses on procedure not outcomes, and internal reviews will occur more frequently.

excerpt: It is possible at some point in the future that another actor in the frontier AI ecosystem will pass, or be on track to imminently pass, a Capability Threshold without implementing measures equivalent to the Required Safeguards such that their actions pose a serious risk for the world.
paraphrase: The footnote considers a future scenario where another AI actor exceeds a Capability Threshold without equivalent safeguards, posing serious world risk.

excerpt: In such a scenario, because the incremental increase in risk attributable to us would be small, we might decide to lower the Required Safeguards.
paraphrase: In that scenario, Anthropic might lower Required Safeguards since its own incremental risk contribution would be small.

excerpt: If we take this measure, however, we will also acknowledge the overall level of risk posed by AI systems (including ours), and will invest significantly in making a case to the U.S. government for taking regulatory action to mitigate such risk to acceptable levels.
paraphrase: If safeguards are lowered under this scenario, Anthropic will acknowledge overall AI risk and advocate for U.S. government regulatory action.

excerpt: We currently expect that if we do not deploy the model publicly and instead proceed with training or limited deployments, we will likely instead share evaluation details with a relevant U.S. Government entity.
paraphrase: For non-public deployments, Anthropic expects to share evaluation details with a relevant U.S. Government entity instead.

excerpt: These will be posted to www.anthropic.com/rsp-updates. We anticipate providing updates at least every 6-12 months.
paraphrase: Updates will be posted online, expected at least every 6-12 months.

excerpt: Where possible, we will include descriptions of the empirical evaluation results we believe would indicate that a model is no longer safe to store under the ASL-2 Standard.
paraphrase: Where feasible, updates will describe evaluation results indicating a model is no longer safe under ASL-2.

excerpt: Our purpose in these updates is to provide sufficient detail to facilitate conversations about best practices for safeguards, capability evaluations, and elicitation.
paraphrase: The purpose of the updates is to enable dialogue on best practices for safeguards, evaluations, and elicitation.

excerpt: Technical and operational standards for safely training and deploying frontier AI models. Higher ASLs correspond to stronger safety and security measures required for more capable models.
paraphrase: ASLs are graded standards for safe training and deployment, with higher levels requiring stronger measures.

excerpt: The current default standard for all Anthropic models, including security measures, safety testing, and automated misuse detection.
paraphrase: ASL-2 is the default standard for all models covering security, safety testing, and misuse detection.

excerpt: A higher level of safeguards required when a model cannot be certified as ASL-2 appropriate. It includes more stringent security and deployment measures designed to mitigate risks from more capable models.
paraphrase: ASL-3 is a stronger safeguard tier for models that no longer qualify as ASL-2 appropriate.

excerpt: A document attesting that a model is sufficiently far from each of the relevant Capability Thresholds, and therefore (still) appropriate for storing under an ASL-N Standard. It includes evaluation procedures, results, and other relevant evidence gathered around the time of testing.
paraphrase: A Capability Report documents that a model remains sufficiently distant from relevant Capability Thresholds, including evaluation evidence.

excerpt: Specific AI capabilities that, if reached, would require stronger safeguards than the current baseline ASL-N standard provides.
paraphrase: Capability Thresholds are specific capabilities that trigger the need for stronger safeguards.

excerpt: A scaling trend-based metric that accounts for both FLOPs and algorithmic improvements.
paraphrase: Effective Compute is a metric combining raw compute and algorithmic efficiency gains.

excerpt: Empirical tests designed to provide early warning when a model is approaching a Capability Threshold. These tests are intended to trigger before a model actually reaches a dangerous capability.
paraphrase: Evaluations are empirical tests meant to warn before a model reaches a dangerous capability.

excerpt: Floating-Point Operation(s). The amount of computation required to train or run a model. The number of FLOPs can be used as one indicator of a model's computational complexity and, indirectly, its potential capabilities.
paraphrase: FLOPs measure computation used to train or run a model and serve as an indirect capability indicator.

excerpt: Anthropic's Board of Directors approves the RSP and receives Capability Reports and Safeguards Reports. The LTBT is an external body that is consulted on policy changes and also provided with Capability Reports and Safeguards Reports.
paraphrase: The Board approves the RSP and receives reports; the LTBT is an external body consulted on changes and also receiving reports.

excerpt: The standard of safety and security measures that must be implemented when a model reaches a Capability Threshold.
paraphrase: Required Safeguards are the mandated measures triggered when a Capability Threshold is reached.

excerpt: A designated staff member responsible for reducing catastrophic risk, primarily by ensuring this policy is designed and implemented effectively. Their duties include reviewing policy updates, approving reports, overseeing implementation, and approving deployments.
paraphrase: The RSO is the staff member tasked with reducing catastrophic risk via policy design/implementation, report approval, and deployment sign-off.

excerpt: A document attesting that the implemented safeguards meet an ASL-N Standard. It details the design and planned implementation of safeguards, and evidence to demonstrate their expected effectiveness.
paraphrase: A Safeguards Report attests that safeguards meet an ASL-N standard, detailing design and evidence of effectiveness.

excerpt: Acceptable use policies and model cards: Publication of model cards for significant new models describing capabilities, limitations, evaluations, and intended use cases.
paraphrase: ASL-2 deployment requires publishing model cards describing capabilities, limitations, evaluations, and intended uses.

excerpt: Enforcement of a Usage Policy that restricts, at a minimum, catastrophic and high harm use cases, including using the model to generate content that could cause severe risks to the continued existence of humankind, or direct and severe harm to individuals.
paraphrase: A Usage Policy is enforced restricting catastrophic and high-harm use cases including existential and severe individual harm content.

excerpt: Harmlessness training and automated detection: Training models to refuse requests to aid in causing harm, such as with Constitutional AI or other improved techniques, and the use of model enhanced trust and safety detection and enforcement.
paraphrase: Models are trained to refuse harmful requests using techniques like Constitutional AI, alongside enhanced trust and safety detection.

excerpt: Fine-tuning protections: In finetuning products, data is filtered for harmfulness, and models are subject to automated evaluation to check harmlessness features are not degraded.
paraphrase: Finetuning products filter harmful data and undergo automated checks to ensure harmlessness features remain intact.

excerpt: There are a very limited number of use cases where this tooling is disabled. These are negotiated on a case by case basis and considered only for extremely low risk use cases that involve company personnel.
paraphrase: Disabling this tooling is limited to rare, individually negotiated, extremely low-risk cases involving company personnel.

excerpt: Vulnerability reporting channels: Clearly indicated paths within the product for users to report harmful or dangerous model outputs, as well as a bug bounty for universal jailbreaks.
paraphrase: Products provide clear reporting paths for harmful outputs and a bug bounty targeting universal jailbreaks.

excerpt: ASL-2 Security Standard: A security system that can likely thwart most opportunistic attackers.
paraphrase: The ASL-2 Security Standard is designed to likely thwart most opportunistic attackers.

excerpt: Supply chain: Vendor and supplier security must be regularly reviewed to ensure that they meet security standards. Software updates should be frequently managed and compliance monitoring automated where possible.
paraphrase: Vendor/supplier security must be regularly reviewed, with frequent software updates and automated compliance monitoring where feasible.

excerpt: Offices: Physical security should entail visitor access logs and restrictions protect on-site assets. Highly sensitive interactions should utilize advanced authentication like security keys.
paraphrase: Physical office security should include visitor logs and access restrictions, with advanced authentication like security keys for sensitive interactions.

excerpt: Network visibility should be maintained and office access controls and communications should maximize on-site protections.
paraphrase: Network visibility and office access controls should be maintained to maximize on-site protection.

excerpt: Workforce: People-critical processes must represent a key aspect of cybersecurity. Mandatory periodic infosec training educates all employees on secure practices, like proper system configurations and strong passwords, and fosters a proactive "security mindset."
paraphrase: Workforce security requires mandatory periodic infosec training covering secure practices and fostering a security mindset.

excerpt: Fundamental infrastructure and policies promoting secure-by-design and secure-by-default principles should be incorporated into the engineering process. An insider risk program should tie access to job roles. Rapid incident response protocols must be deployed.
paraphrase: Secure-by-design principles should be built into engineering, an insider risk program should tie access to roles, and rapid incident response must be deployed.

excerpt: Compartmentalization: Segmented system isolation must ensure limited blast radius. Features like zero trust architecture should require access from approved devices.
paraphrase: System isolation must limit blast radius, and zero trust architecture should restrict access to approved devices.

excerpt: Strict protocols must be deployed to regulate weight copies on company networks and limit storage to only approved, restricted systems.
paraphrase: Strict protocols must regulate weight copies and restrict storage to approved systems.

excerpt: Infrastructure: Standard security infrastructure, monitoring software, access management tools, and disk encryption provide a technology baseline.
paraphrase: A technology baseline includes standard security infrastructure, monitoring, access management, and disk encryption.

excerpt: Process elements like incident reporting procedures, lost/stolen device protocols and Detection and Response should support these. External validation like SOC 2 compliance and continuous vulnerability management must ensure adaptations match infosec developments.
paraphrase: Supporting processes include incident reporting, device loss protocols, and Detection and Response, alongside SOC 2 validation and vulnerability management.
